summary: The quasi-split unramified Grothendieck–Serre theorem is reduced through geometric presentation, excision and affine-line torsors to corrected field and Whitehead arguments. The two proposed Part II directions import relative reductive-group foundations and scheme/descent foundations without rebuilding them. The full main paper is read and its numbered results are split below. Complete (cc-442dc5): seven mistakes are recorded, three already corrected in print (the p. 20 footnote, Gille 2005, Gille 2026) and four new. The new gap in the loop-coset step of Proposition 8.4 is repaired by one added item. Supplier proofs remain for the design jobs; this is not a formalization.

items.statement: The central torus rad(G) of reductive G/R is isotrivial if it becomes split after some faithfully flat finite étale R-algebra.

items.name: Borel torus is quasi-trivial
items.statement: If S is a scheme, G/S semisimple simply connected or adjoint, and T⊂B⊂G a maximal torus in a Borel, then T≅Res_{S'/S}G_m for a finite étale S-scheme S', the Dynkin scheme.

items.name: Vanishing for semilocal quasi-trivial tori
items.statement: In Lemma 2.1, if S is affine semilocal, H1(S,T)≅H1(S',G_m)=Pic(S')=0.

items.name: Reduction to the simply-connected derived group
items.statement: Let R be Noetherian semilocal with every prime's strict henselization a UFD, K its total fractions, and G quasi-split reductive. Trivial kernel for H1(R,(G_der)_sc)→H1(K,(G_der)_sc) implies trivial kernel for H1(R,G)→H1(K,G).

items.name: Relative hypersurface avoidance
items.statement: For any ring R, quasi-projective finitely presented X/R, very R-ample L, finitely presented closed Z containing no positive-dimensional component of any R-fiber, and finitely many y_i∉Z, there is N0 such that every N≥N0 admits h∈Γ(X,L^N) whose hypersurface contains Z and avoids the y_i and all such fiber components.

items.name: Prescribed-locus Bertini dimension
items.statement: Let k be any field, X/k projective of pure dimension d, L ample, Y1,…,Ym,Z closed, Z=Z1⊔Z0 with Z0 reduced zero-dimensional in X_sm and all its residue extensions separable, and 0≤t≤min(d,d−dim Z). There are hypersurfaces H1,…,Ht with intersection of pure dimension d−t containing Z.

items.name: Prescribed-locus Bertini smoothness
items.statement: Let k be any field, X/k projective of pure dimension d, L ample, Y1,…,Ym,Z closed, Z=Z1⊔Z0 with Z0 reduced zero-dimensional in X_sm and all its residue extensions separable, and 0≤t≤min(d,d−dim Z). The hypersurfaces may simultaneously be chosen so that (X_sm\Z1)∩H1∩…∩Ht is k-smooth.

items.name: Bertini dimension drop for all subsets
items.statement: Let k be any field, X/k projective of pure dimension d, L ample, Y1,…,Ym,Z closed, Z=Z1⊔Z0 with Z0 reduced zero-dimensional in X_sm and all its residue extensions separable, and 0≤t≤min(d,d−dim Z). The same choice satisfies dim((Y_j\Z)∩⋂_{l∈I}H_l)≤dim(Y_j\Z)−|I| for every j and every subset I⊂{1,…,t}.

items.name: Iterative Bertini degree control
items.statement: Let k be any field, X/k projective of pure dimension d, L ample, Y1,…,Ym,Z closed, Z=Z1⊔Z0 with Z0 reduced zero-dimensional in X_sm and all its residue extensions separable, and 0≤t≤min(d,d−dim Z). With earlier H_i fixed, each next degree may be any sufficiently large multiple of the characteristic exponent of k. Equal degrees for all H_i are not asserted.

items.name: Nonempty intersections attain the dimension bound
items.statement: Under Lemma 3.2(iii), if (Y_j\Z)∩⋂_{l∈I}H_l is nonempty, its dimension equals dim(Y_j\Z)−|I|.

items.name: Weight-one affine chart
items.statement: For any scheme S and positive weights with w0=1, D_+(t0)⊂P_S(1,w1,…,wd) is A^d_S with coordinates t_i/t0^{w_i}.

items.name: Weighted blowup away from its center
items.statement: The weighted blowup of §3.5 is an isomorphism over X minus the common zero scheme of its defining sections.

items.name: Equal weights recover ordinary blowup
items.statement: If all weights are equal, the weighted blowup is canonically the ordinary blowup along the ideal cut out by the sections.

items.name: Weighted projection (i)
items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. One common choice satisfies H0 avoids all x_i.

items.name: Weighted projection (ii)
items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. One common choice satisfies Y∩H0∩…∩H_{d−1}=∅.

items.name: Weighted projection (iii)
items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. One common choice satisfies π is smooth of relative dimension 1 at every x_i.

items.name: Weighted projection (iv)
items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. One common choice satisfies For each i, Y∩H0∩π^{-1}(π(x_i))=∅.

items.name: Weighted projection (v)
items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. One common choice satisfies If codim_X(Y\X_sm)>1, π is smooth at every point of Y over each π(x_i).

items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. One common choice satisfies If codim_X(Y\W)>1, (Y\W)∩π^{-1}(π(x_i))=∅ for all i.

items.name: Weighted projection (vii)
items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. One common choice satisfies If codim_X(Y\W)>1, there are affine opens S⊂A^{d−1}_k and U⊂W∩π^{-1}S⊂X\H0 containing all x_i, such that π:U→S is smooth of relative dimension 1 and Y∩U=Y∩π^{-1}S is finite over S.

items.name: Weighted projection degree control
items.statement: Let k be a field, X/k projective of pure dimension d>0, L ample, W⊂X_sm open, finitely many x_i∈W, and Y⊂X closed of positive codimension. After replacing L by any sufficiently large power, choose h0∈Γ(L) and nonzero h_j∈Γ(L^{w_j}), 1≤j<d, with positive w_j. Write H_j=V(h_j) and π for the weighted projection, extended to the weighted blowup. Each next section can be chosen with any sufficiently large degree divisible by the characteristic exponent, once preceding sections are fixed.

items.name: Dedekind-base weighted projection (i)
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The conclusions of Proposition 3.6(i) hold over O for a common weighted projection, with codimension conditions interpreted fiberwise: H0 avoids all x_i.

items.name: Dedekind-base weighted projection (ii)
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The conclusions of Proposition 3.6(ii) hold over O for a common weighted projection, with codimension conditions interpreted fiberwise: Y∩H0∩…∩H_{d−1}=∅.

items.name: Dedekind-base weighted projection (iii)
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The conclusions of Proposition 3.6(iii) hold over O for a common weighted projection, with codimension conditions interpreted fiberwise: π is smooth of relative dimension 1 at every x_i.

items.name: Dedekind-base weighted projection (iv)
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The conclusions of Proposition 3.6(iv) hold over O for a common weighted projection, with codimension conditions interpreted fiberwise: For each i, Y∩H0∩π^{-1}(π(x_i))=∅.

items.name: Dedekind-base weighted projection (v)
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The conclusions of Proposition 3.6(v) hold over O for a common weighted projection, with codimension conditions interpreted fiberwise: If fiberwise codim_X(Y\X_sm)>1, π is smooth at every point of Y over each π(x_i).

items.name: Dedekind-base weighted projection (vi)
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The conclusions of Proposition 3.6(vi) hold over O for a common weighted projection, with codimension conditions interpreted fiberwise: If fiberwise codim_X(Y\W)>1, (Y\W)∩π^{-1}(π(x_i))=∅ for all i.

items.name: Dedekind-base weighted projection (vii)
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The conclusions of Proposition 3.6(vii) hold over O for a common weighted projection, with codimension conditions interpreted fiberwise: If fiberwise codim_X(Y\W)>1, there are affine opens S⊂A^{d−1}_O and U⊂W∩π^{-1}S⊂X\H0 containing all x_i, such that π:U→S is smooth of relative dimension 1 and Y∩U=Y∩π^{-1}S is finite over S.

items.name: Dedekind projection successive degree bounds
items.statement: Let O be a semilocal Dedekind ring, X/O projective and flat with pure d-dimensional fibers (d>0), L relatively ample, W⊂X_sm/O open containing finitely many x_i, and Y closed of positive codimension in every O-fiber. The sections can be chosen successively with the sufficiently-large divisibility conditions simultaneously required by the residue-field constructions.

items.name: Smooth curve fibration through finitely many points
items.statement: For semilocal Dedekind O, a smooth O-algebra A everywhere of positive relative dimension, finitely many x_i∈Spec A and closed Y of total codimension≥2, there are affine opens U⊂Spec A containing all x_i and S⊂⨿_{d≥0}A^d_O and a smooth O-map U→S of pure relative dimension 1 with Y∩U finite over S.

items.name: Lift a torsor to a relative curve
items.statement: Let O be semilocal Dedekind, R the semilocalization at finitely many primes of a smooth O-algebra, G/R quasi-split reductive, B⊂G a Borel, and E a generically trivial right G-torsor. There exist smooth affine R-curve C of pure relative dimension 1, section s, R-finite closed Z⊂C, quasi-split reductive Gcal/C with Borel Bcal, and a Gcal-torsor Ecal, whose s-pullbacks are respectively G,B,E.

items.name: Unipotent reduction off the finite locus
items.statement: Let O be semilocal Dedekind, R the semilocalization at finitely many primes of a smooth O-algebra, G/R quasi-split reductive, B⊂G a Borel, and E a generically trivial right G-torsor. The data of Proposition 4.2 may be chosen with Ecal|C\Z induced from an Ru(Bcal)-torsor.

items.name: Compatible quasi-pinnings on the curve
items.statement: Let O be semilocal Dedekind, R the semilocalization at finitely many primes of a smooth O-algebra, G/R quasi-split reductive, B⊂G a Borel, and E a generically trivial right G-torsor. For any chosen quasi-pinning of G extending B, Proposition 4.2's Gcal can be quasi-pinned compatibly with s-pullback.

items.name: Field-base curve lifting without quasi-splitness
items.statement: When O is a field in the smooth-semilocal setup of Proposition 4.2, the quasi-split assumption can be omitted and Ecal can be made trivial on C\Z.

items.name: Quasi-pinned isomorphisms form a locally constant étale scheme
items.statement: For quasi-pinned reductive groups of the same geometric type over A, the functor of quasi-pinning-preserving isomorphisms is represented by an étale-locally constant scheme.

items.name: Finite étale extension of a prescribed isomorphism
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian semilocal with geometrically unibranch localizations, I⊂A an ideal, G,G' reductive of the same geometric types with quasi-pinnings, and ι:G_A/I≅G'_A/I preserving them. There exist faithfully flat finite étale A-algebra Atilde, A/I-point a, and a quasi-pinning-preserving isomorphism over Atilde restricting to ι via a.

items.name: Make the curve group constant
items.statement: Let O be semilocal Dedekind, R the semilocalization at finitely many primes of a smooth O-algebra, G/R quasi-split reductive, B⊂G a Borel, and E a generically trivial right G-torsor. There exist smooth affine relative curve C, section s, R-finite closed Z and a G_C-torsor Ecal pulling back to E and reducing to Ru(B)_C on C\Z.

items.name: Finite cover with residue-point room
items.statement: For semilocal R, quasi-projective finitely presented C/R, R-finite closed Z⊂C and s∈Z(R), there is finite Ctilde→C, étale above Z, with a lift of s, such that for every finite closed residue field k_m and every d≥1 the number of degree-d points of Ztilde_km is strictly less than that of A1_km.

items.name: Residue extensions on smooth curves are simple
items.statement: If C is a smooth connected curve over any field k and c∈C is closed, then k_c/k is a simple finite extension.

items.name: Corrected embedding of first-order neighborhoods
items.statement: For the residue curves in Lemma 6.3, the disjoint first-order neighborhoods ε_z=Spec(O_Ckm/I_z²) of the finitely many closed points of Z_km admit a closed immersion into A1_km, with distinct images chosen as required by the point-count construction.
items.note: The printed step (E1) takes the Cohen-structure isomorphism for a k_m-isomorphism; this item states what the author's post-publication footnote proves instead.

items.name: Flat affine-line presentation
items.statement: Let R be semilocal, C/R flat affine with Cohen–Macaulay pure one-dimensional fibers, Y⊂C finite over R, and Z⊂C_sm finite over R. For every finite closed residue field k_m and d≥1 assume #Z_km(degree d)<#A1_km(degree d). There exist open C'⊂C containing Y and Z, and quasi-finite flat R-map f:C'→A1_R, étale along Z, mapping Z isomorphically onto a closed Z'⊂A1_R with Z=C'×A1 Z'.

items.name: All infinitesimal neighborhoods agree
items.statement: Let R be semilocal, C/R flat affine with Cohen–Macaulay pure one-dimensional fibers, Y⊂C finite over R, and Z⊂C_sm finite over R. For every finite closed residue field k_m and d≥1 assume #Z_km(degree d)<#A1_km(degree d). For the chosen f of Lemma 6.3, the induced maps on every infinitesimal neighborhood of Z⊂C' and Z'⊂A1_R are isomorphisms.

items.name: Nonstrict point count when the retained locus lies in Z
items.statement: In Lemma 6.3 the point-count inequalities may be weakened to ≤ if every closed point of Y belongs to Z.

items.name: Finite locally free subschemes of the affine line are monic
items.statement: If Spec R is connected and Z'⊂A1_R is finite locally free of rank n, then its defining ideal is generated by a monic polynomial of degree n.

items.name: Torsor on a presented curve
items.statement: Let O be semilocal Dedekind, R the semilocalization at finitely many primes of a smooth O-algebra, G/R quasi-split reductive, B⊂G a Borel, and E a generically trivial right G-torsor. One may choose the constant-group data of Proposition 5.2 together with a flat map C→A1_R mapping Z isomorphically to closed Z'⊂A1_R and giving a cartesian square along Z.

items.name: Flat-neighborhood patching for torsors
items.statement: Let S'→S be affine flat and an isomorphism over closed Z cut out by a quasi-coherent finite-type ideal; put U=S\Z and U'=U×S S'. For quasi-affine flat finitely presented G/S, G-torsors are equivalent to triples (E_S',E_U,an isomorphism over U').

items.name: Flat excision for quasi-coherent support cohomology
items.statement: For a flat map S'→S of affine Noetherian schemes inducing an isomorphism over closed Z, and any quasi-coherent O_S-module F or complex of such modules, RΓ_Z(S,F)→RΓ_Z(S',F_S') is an isomorphism.

items.name: Kernel triviality for filtered smooth groups
items.statement: Under Lemma 7.2's square, if F is an affine smooth S-group with a finite filtration by normal affine smooth S-subgroups having vector-bundle group quotients, H1(U,F)→H1(U',F) has trivial kernel.

items.name: Surjectivity for centrally filtered groups
items.statement: Under Lemma 7.2's square, if F is an affine smooth U-group with a finite filtration by normal affine smooth U-subgroups whose vector-group quotients are central in the corresponding quotients of F, H1(U,F)→H1(U',F) is surjective.

items.name: Parabolic radicals admit central vector filtrations
items.statement: The unipotent radical of a parabolic subgroup of a reductive S-group has the affine smooth central vector-group filtration needed in both versions of Lemma 7.2(b).

items.name: Reduction to a torsor on the affine line
items.statement: Let O be semilocal Dedekind, R the semilocalization at finitely many primes of a smooth O-algebra, G/R quasi-split reductive, B⊂G a Borel, and E a generically trivial right G-torsor. There are finite closed Z⊂A1_R and a G_A1-torsor Ecal with zero-section pullback E and trivial restriction to A1_R\Z.

items.name: Quasi-split implies total isotropy
items.statement: Every quasi-split reductive group scheme is totally isotropic.

items.name: Fiberwise trivial vector bundles on a semilocal projective line
items.statement: Let R be semilocal. A rank-n vector bundle on P1_R whose restriction to every P1_km is trivial is itself trivial.

items.name: Projective-line torsors descend to the semilocal base
items.statement: Let R be semilocal, G reductive with rad(G) split by a finite étale cover, and E a G_P1-torsor trivial on P1_km for each maximal m. Then E is pulled back from a G-torsor over R.

items.name: Simultaneous lifting in opposite unipotent radicals
items.statement: For semilocal R and a parabolic P of reductive G with opposite P−, both Ru(P)(R((t)))→∏_m Ru(P)(k_m((t))) and its opposite version are surjective.

items.name: Loop lifts from a parabolic over one local ring
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian semilocal ring, G an affine smooth R-group, m ⊂ R a maximal ideal, and U ⊂ G_{R_m} a closed subscheme with an isomorphism of R_m-schemes A^d_{R_m} ≅ U sending 0 to 1. Then every element of U(k_m((t))) is the image of some g ∈ G(R((t))) whose image in G(k_{m′}((t))) is 1 for every maximal ideal m′ ≠ m.
items.locator: Proposition 8.4 proof, claim (2): repair recorded under E4 (not in the paper)
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5. The paper's claim (2) lifts elements of R_u(P)(k_m((t))) for a single proper parabolic P over R, which total isotropy does not supply when R is semilocal but not local (E4).

items.name: Surjectivity of residue loop cosets
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian semilocal ring and G a semisimple, simply connected R-group with simple geometric fibres such that, for every maximal ideal m ⊂ R, G_{R_m} has a proper parabolic subgroup. Then G(R((t)))/G(R[[t]]) → ∏_m G(k_m((t)))/G(k_m[[t]]) is surjective.
items.locator: Proposition 8.4 proof, claim (2), with the repair of E4
items.note: Corrected statement (cc-442dc5, E4). The printed argument assumes a proper parabolic over R, which Definition 8.1 supplies only over the local rings. The Noetherian hypothesis is what the repair uses; Proposition 8.4 itself is reduced to Noetherian R by a limit argument.

items.name: Totally isotropic affine-line torsors are trivial
items.statement: For any semilocal ring R and totally isotropic semisimple simply-connected reductive G/R, a G_A1-torsor trivial away from an R-finite closed subscheme Z⊂A1_R is trivial.
items.note: Statement as printed. The printed proof of claim (2) needs a proper parabolic over R (E4); the repair goes through loop-coset-surjective in its corrected Noetherian form. For quasi-split G, as in Theorem 9.1, the printed argument applies directly.

items.name: Quasi-split unramified Grothendieck–Serre
items.statement: For Dedekind O, regular semilocal flat O-algebra R with geometrically regular fibers, and quasi-split reductive G/R, ker(H1(R,G)→H1(Frac(R),G))={*}.

items.name: Perfect-field instance
items.statement: If O is a perfect field and R a regular semilocal O-algebra, every quasi-split reductive generically trivial R-torsor is trivial.

items.name: Integer-base criterion
items.statement: For a regular semilocal Z-flat ring R, geometric regularity of its Z-fibers is equivalent to p∉m² for every prime p and maximal ideal m of residue characteristic p.

items.name: Local quasi-split unramified theorem
items.statement: If R is an unramified regular local ring and G/R is quasi-split reductive, every generically trivial G-torsor is trivial.

items.name: Generic splitness descends
items.statement: For O and R as in Theorem 9.1 and any reductive R-group G, G is split if and only if G_Frac(R) is split.

items.name: Local generic-split criterion
items.statement: A reductive group over an unramified regular local ring is split if and only if its generic fiber is split.

items.name: Principal-completion factorization
items.statement: For unramified regular local R, quasi-split reductive G/R and nonzero r∈R, with r-adic completion Rhat, G(Rhat[1/r])=G(Rhat)·G(R[1/r]).

items.name: Conditional generic quasi-split descent
items.statement: Let R be regular semilocal, K=Frac(R), and G reductive. Assume every R-form H of G_ad satisfies injectivity H1(R,H)→H1(K,H). Then G is quasi-split if and only if G_K is quasi-split.

items.name: Equicharacteristic generic quasi-split descent
items.statement: For a regular semilocal ring containing a field and reductive G/R, G is quasi-split if and only if G_Frac(R) is quasi-split.

items.name: Special orthogonal torsor injectivity
items.statement: Let R be as in Theorem 9.1 with 2 invertible and K=Frac(R). For every n≥1, H1(R,SO_n)→H1(K,SO_n) is injective. SO_n and O_n are the split orthogonal groups in the source's convention.
items.note: The proof twists SO_n by SO_n-torsors, whose twists are the SO(E). The printed claim that every inner form of SO_n is an SO(E) is false for even n ≥ 4 but is not used beyond these twists (E7).

items.name: Orthogonal torsor injectivity
items.statement: Let R be as in Theorem 9.1 with 2 invertible and K=Frac(R). For every n≥1, H1(R,O_n)→H1(K,O_n) is injective. SO_n and O_n are the split orthogonal groups in the source's convention.

items.name: Generic isometry descends
items.statement: Let R be as in Theorem 9.1 with 2 invertible and K=Frac(R). For every n≥1, two nondegenerate quadratic forms over R whose associated symmetric bilinear forms are perfect and which become isomorphic over K are isomorphic over R. SO_n and O_n are the split orthogonal groups in the source's convention.

items.name: Finite-type relative Proj
items.statement: For a finitely generated graded quasi-coherent O_S-algebra, use the relative Proj construction of Stable Reduction Layer 2, with canonical affine-base agreement with Mathlib's absolute Proj.

api.statement: Expose the structural morphism and homogeneous basic opens.

api.name: GrothendieckSerre.relative_proj.api2
api.statement: Compare with the affine-base absolute construction.

api.name: GrothendieckSerre.relative_proj.api3
api.statement: Use its base-change and invertible-sheaf-twist comparisons.

items.name: Proper-curve cohomology and base change
items.statement: Use the full cohomology-and-base-change theorem for coherent sheaves on proper relative curves over locally Noetherian bases, as owned by Stable Reduction Layer 2; in §8.3 apply it to the Hom bundle on P1 and vanishing of its fiber H1.

items.name: Semilocal Picard vanishing
items.statement: An invertible module over a semilocal ring is free of rank 1; hence Pic(Spec R)=0.

items.name: Finite étale Shapiro for torsors
items.statement: For finite étale S'→S and the affine group schemes used here, H1(S,Res_{S'/S}G')≅H1(S',G'), compatibly with base change and trivial classes.

items.name: Generic injectivity for torus torsors
items.statement: For the Noetherian semilocal R with factorial strict henselizations in Proposition 2.2 and an R-torus T, H1(R,T)→H1(Frac(R),T) is injective.
items.locator: CTS87 Theorem 4.1, as used in CES22 §§2.2,4.2

items.name: Generic H2 injectivity for multiplicative-type kernels
items.statement: For the Noetherian semilocal R of Proposition 2.2 and a finite multiplicative-type R-group Z, H2_fppf(R,Z)→H2_fppf(Frac(R),Z) is injective.
items.locator: CTS87 Theorem 4.3, as used in CES22 Proposition 2.2

items.name: Codimension-two purity for torus torsors
items.statement: For regular locally Noetherian X, open U with complement of codimension≥2, and an X-torus T, restriction H1(X,T)→H1(U,T) is a bijection in the purity setting used in the paper.

items.name: Strict henselizations of regular local rings are factorial
items.statement: Strict henselizations of regular local rings are regular local and hence UFDs; regular semilocal rings meet Proposition 2.2's condition at every prime.

items.name: Fiberwise Cohen–Macaulay flatness in the presentation lemma
items.statement: In Lemma 6.3, an R-morphism from R-flat C with pure one-dimensional Cohen–Macaulay fibers to A1_R which is quasi-finite is flat.

items.name: Finite components of locally constant étale schemes
items.statement: Over Noetherian geometrically unibranch A, the connected components of an étale-locally constant A-scheme are open and finite étale over A, as used for the isomorphism scheme in Lemma 5.1.
items.locator: SGA3 II X5.14 with EGAI6.1.9; CES22 Lemma 5.1 proof

items.name: Extend generic sections of finite étale schemes
items.statement: Over a normal integral affine base R, a K-point of a finite étale R-scheme extends uniquely to an R-point. Apply componentwise to the locally constant Out-torsor in Theorem 9.3.

items.name: Projectivity of the twisted Borel quotient
items.statement: For reductive G/S, Borel B⊂G and G-torsor E, E/B is represented by a projective S-scheme; over a regular integral base a generic section extends across every codimension-one point.
items.locator: Proposition 4.2 and Theorem 9.5 proofs; SGA3 XXVI3.6,3.20

items.name: Pinned split automorphism extension
items.statement: For split reductive G/S with fixed pinning, 1→G_ad→Aut(G)→Out(G)→1 is split by pinning-preserving automorphisms and Out(G) is constant.

items.name: Borel-preserving automorphism extension
items.statement: For split pinned G with Borel B, the extension 1→B_ad→Aut(G,B)→Out(G)→1 embeds in the Aut(G) extension and admits a compatible pinning splitting.

items.name: Central nonabelian obstruction sequence
items.statement: For a central extension 1→A→F→Q→1 of sheaves with A abelian, the pointed H1 sequence ends in an obstruction H1(Q)→H2(A); the exactness and twisting action give the lifting criterion used in Lemma 7.2.

items.name: Affine vector-group acyclicity
items.statement: For an affine scheme S and quasi-coherent O_S-module M, the sheaf cohomology used for vector groups satisfies H^i(S,M)=0 for every i>0.
items.locator: Lemma 7.2 and Proposition 7.4 proofs; SGA3 XXVI2.3

items.name: Flat-neighborhood local-cohomology base change
items.statement: For A→A' flat between Noetherian rings and a finitely generated ideal I with A/I≅A'/IA', supported cohomology base changes derivedly and every I-power-torsion cohomology module maps isomorphically to its A'-tensor product.

items.name: Moret-Bailly patching for quasi-affine-diagonal stacks
items.statement: Under the flat affine neighborhood square of Lemma 7.1 with finite-type defining ideal, an algebraic stack with quasi-affine diagonal has its category of S-objects equivalent to the category of compatible objects over S' and U.

items.name: Effective quasi-affine patching
items.statement: In the Moret-Bailly flat neighborhood situation, compatible quasi-affine spaces patch effectively, by the canonical fpqc descent datum and effectiveness of fpqc descent for quasi-affine spaces.

items.name: Formal gluing at infinity for affine-group torsors
items.statement: For semilocal R and affine finitely presented G/R in Proposition 8.4, glue torsors on A1_R and Spec R[[t]] along Spec R((t)), with t inverse to the A1 coordinate, obtaining a G-torsor on P1_R.

items.name: Linearity criterion for reductive groups
items.statement: For semilocal R and reductive G/R, the isotrivial-radical condition in Lemma 8.3 is equivalent to a closed embedding G→GL_n for some n.
items.locator: Lemma 8.3 proof; Gil21 Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 4.3

items.name: Affineness of GLn/G
items.statement: For a closed reductive subgroup G⊂GL_n over the base in Lemma 8.3, the quotient GL_n/G is affine.

items.name: Maps from the relative projective line to an affine target
items.statement: For affine R-scheme X, every R-map P1_R→X factors uniquely through Spec R.

items.name: Semilocal parabolic radicals are affine spaces
items.statement: For a parabolic P of a reductive group over semilocal R, Ru(P) is isomorphic as an R-scheme to a finite-rank affine space (with rank componentwise if needed), as is the radical of an opposite parabolic.

items.name: Popescu approximation
items.statement: Every regular homomorphism of Noetherian rings is a filtered colimit of smooth ring maps.

items.name: Descend finite-presentation group and torsor data
items.statement: Along the filtered smooth O-algebras approximating R in Theorem 9.1, reductive G, its quasi-pinning, a torsor E and a trivialization over R[1/r] descend after advancing the index; semilocalization at the finitely many image primes preserves the required data.

items.name: Full equicharacteristic Grothendieck–Serre input
items.statement: For a regular semilocal ring containing a field and every reductive group over it, a generically trivial torsor is trivial; applying this to inner forms yields H1 injectivity.
items.locator: Theorem 9.5 parenthesis; FP15 and Pan20a cited in §1.4

items.name: Quadratic forms and orthogonal torsor classes
items.statement: Over semilocal R with 2 invertible, isometry classes of rank-n nondegenerate quadratic spaces are classified by H1(R,O_n) after choosing the split reference form; inner forms of SO_n are SO(E).

items.name: Cancellation reduction to hyperbolic generic triviality
items.statement: In the semilocal 2-invertible setting of CT79 Proposition 1.2, the isometry-descent property in Corollary 9.6 is equivalent to trivial kernel for split O_n in all even ranks, and those kernels agree with the corresponding split SO_n kernel question.

items.name: Gabber–Gros–Suwa geometric presentation
items.statement: Let k be infinite, X a smooth affine irreducible k-variety of dimension d>0, finitely many points t_i of X, and Z⊂X a closed subvariety of positive codimension. There are φ=(ψ,ν):X→A^{d−1}×A1, opens V⊂A^{d−1} and U⊂ψ^{-1}V containing the t_i, such that Z∩U=Z∩ψ^{-1}V, ψ|Z is finite, φ|U is étale, Z∩U maps by closed immersion to A1_V, φ(t_i)∉φ(Z) whenever t_i∉Z, and φ^{-1}(φ(Z∩U))∩U=Z∩U. The infinitesimal-thickening application is the one explicitly made in CES22's correction.

items.name: Open conditions for finite and étale projection
items.statement: In CTHK97's affine-embedding setup, the coefficient choices making projection finite on the prescribed divisor and étale at the marked smooth points contain a nonempty open in the affine parameter space.

items.name: Projection separates the prescribed finite fibers
items.statement: In CTHK97's parameter construction, radiciality/separation over the marked fibers and avoidance of unwanted intersections hold on a nonempty open, descending from the algebraic closure to k.

items.name: Finite-neighborhood shrinking gives the cartesian square
items.statement: After the projection conditions of CTHK97 §3.4, shrinking around the marked base points gives a closed immersion of the finite divisor into A1_V; removing the nonétale and extra inverse-image loci yields the étale cartesian square.

items.name: Positive-characteristic differential Bertini input
items.statement: For Lemma 3.2's projective pure-dimensional X in characteristic p>0, prescribed first jets along the separable reduced Z0 and values along Z1 and the avoided points can be realized in every sufficiently large degree divisible by p, with smooth zero locus off a finite additional set; a p-th-power perturbation removes that finite set.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2 proof; Gab01 Theorem 1.1 and Corollaries 1.6–1.7 as adapted in footnote 2

items.name: Triviality on affine charts of a normalized projective-line torsor
items.statement: Let k be a field and G/k connected reductive. A G-torsor on P1_k trivial at infinity is trivial on A1_k and also on P1_k\{0}.
items.locator: Gil02 Lemma 3.12, corrected by Gil05 p.269; CES22 §8.4(1)
items.note: Gille's 2002 proof has the gap recorded as E2, repaired in Gil05.

items.name: Anisotropic projective-line case
items.statement: For semisimple k-group G and a G-torsor on P1_k trivial at infinity, if its generic inner form is anisotropic then the torsor is trivial and G is anisotropic.

items.name: Corrected descent of the generic parabolic type
items.statement: In the isotropic branch of Gil02 Lemma 3.12, the parabolic type of the generic inner form specializes, by properness and the normalization at infinity, to a type defined for the original k-group; the Borel/Levi reduction must use this type descent.

items.name: Projective-line torus cohomology calculation
items.statement: For a k-torus T there is a natural split exact sequence 0→H1(k,T)→H1(P1_k,T)→Hom_k(G_m,T)→0. The splitting sends λ to the T-torsor obtained by pushing the Hopf bundle O(−1) forward by −λ, identifying the cocharacter group with H1_Zar(P1_k,T). The cocharacter component restricts trivially to either standard affine chart, while evaluation at infinity detects the constant component.

items.name: Harder's anisotropic generic-fiber rigidity
items.statement: A semisimple group scheme over P1_k whose generic fiber is anisotropic is constant, in the precise Harder theorem quoted in Gil02 Theorem 3.6.
items.locator: Gil02 Theorem 3.6 quoting Har67; application in Lemma 3.7

items.name: Opposite radicals generate the elementary subgroup
items.statement: For infinite F and isotropic semisimple simply-connected absolutely almost simple H/F, H(F)^+ is generated by Ru(P)(F) and Ru(P−)(F) for a proper parabolic P and opposite P−.

items.name: Unramified Whitehead factorization
items.statement: Let O be a henselian DVR with fraction field F, and H a semisimple simply-connected O-group whose special fiber is absolutely almost simple and isotropic. Then H(F)=H(F)^+H(O).
items.locator: Gil09 Lemma 4.5(1), with author errata dated 2026-05-26
items.note: Gille's 2009 proof has the gap recorded as E3, repaired in his 2026 errata.

items.name: Whitehead congruence kernel
items.statement: Under Gil09 Lemma 4.5's henselian-DVR hypotheses, ker(H(O)→H(k)) is contained in H(F)^+.

items.name: Repair of the centralizer-quotient anisotropy step
items.statement: For M=Z_H(S)/S in Gil09 Lemma 4.5, anisotropy of M_k implies anisotropy of M_F: M_F has neither a proper parabolic nor a nontrivial split central torus.

items.name: Split torus points lie in the elementary subgroup
items.statement: In the isotropic simply-connected setting of the corrected Gil09 Lemma 4.5, the relevant maximal split torus S(F) lies in H(F)^+.
items.locator: Gil09 Lemma 4.5 proof; errata replacing Borel–Tits Proposition 6.11 by Corollary 6.8

items.name: Integral points exhaust anisotropic generic points
items.statement: If O is a henselian DVR and M/O is reductive with anisotropic generic fiber, then M(O)=M(Frac O).
items.locator: Guo20 arXivv3 Proposition 3.5(b); published numbering Proposition 6 cited by Gille's errata

items.name: Reductive integral model and maximal parahoric
items.statement: For reductive G over a henselian DVR R, G(R^sh) is a maximal parahoric subgroup of G(K^sh), where R^sh is the strict henselization and K^sh its fraction field, attached to the reductive integral model.

items.name: Semilocal Dedekind group factorization
items.statement: For reductive G over semilocal Dedekind R with fraction field K and the completed DVRs R_v at its maximal ideals, ∏_v G(K_v)=G(K)·∏_v G(R_v).

items.name: Open normal subgroup inside the rational-point closure
items.statement: In Guo20's semilocal Dedekind approximation setup, the closure of diagonal G(K) in ∏G(K_v) contains an open normal subgroup of that product.

items.name: Unipotent-radical contraction in local approximation
items.statement: In Guo20's approximation setup the local unipotent radicals of the chosen parabolics lie in the open normal subgroup obtained from the rational-point closure.

items.name: Complete-DVR anisotropic torsor step
items.statement: For complete DVR R and semisimple anisotropic reductive G/R, a G-torsor trivial over K=Frac R is trivial over R.

items.name: Grothendieck–Serre over semilocal Dedekind rings
items.statement: For semilocal Dedekind R, total fraction ring K and arbitrary reductive G/R, H1_ét(R,G)→H1_ét(K,G) is injective.
items.locator: Guo20 arXivv3 Theorem 1.2; CES22 cites Theorem 1

items.name: Uniqueness of reductive models from adjoint-form injectivity
items.statement: For regular semilocal R, if H1(R,H)→H1(K,H) is injective for every form H of G_ad, then H1(R,Aut G)→H1(K,Aut G) is injective; in particular G is the unique reductive R-model of its generic fiber up to isomorphism.
items.locator: Guo20 arXivv3 Corollary 6.2 with Proposition 6.1; CES22 Theorem 9.5 cites Proposition 14

items.name: Affine vanishing for vector-filtered groups
items.statement: An affine smooth group over an affine scheme, equipped with a finite filtration by normal affine smooth subgroups with vector-bundle group quotients, has trivial H1.
